nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 3$, the real number $\cos(2\pi/n)$ is constructible (it lies in the smallest subfield of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under square roots) if and only if $n$ is a Gauss–Wantzel number, that is, every prime factor of $n$ is $2$ or a Fermat prime and every odd prime factor of $n$ divides $n$ only once.
nodes.title: Gauss–Wantzel theorem

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is a Gauss–Wantzel number if $n > 0$, every prime factor of $n$ is either $2$ or a Fermat prime, and $p^2$ does not divide $n$ for every odd prime factor $p$ of $n$.
nodes.title: Gauss–Wantzel number

nodes.summary: The constructible real numbers form the smallest set of real numbers that contains every rational number and is closed under addition, negation, multiplication, inverses of nonzero elements and square roots of nonnegative elements; equivalently, the smallest subfield of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under square roots.
nodes.title: Constructible real numbers
